trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes up-right.

Going left would leave both cell (0,-3) and number 12 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-right.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
Number 7 is only reachable this way.

Going up-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Going down-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,2); going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,2). So the line goes right.
Going up-right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go left: up-right is number 17, which comes later.

Going up-left would leave both cell (-3,0) and cell (-2,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-right would turn number 11 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
Going down-right would leave number 14 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-right.
Number 14 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 17 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going up-right would leave both number 20 and number 19 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down-left.
Number 17 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 10 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 4/37 cells (11%).
Generation 3: fitness 6/37. The best line covers 8 cells, the first 6 of them still look solvable.
Generation 5: fitness 12/37. The best line covers 15 cells, the first 12 of them still look solvable.
Generation 6: fitness 13/37. The best line covers 16 cells, the first 13 of them still look solvable.
Generation 10: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 10: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 96 futures: 75% survive going up-right (best covers 35%); left 0%; down-left 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 67% survive going up-right (best covers 32%); up-left 0%.
Tried 96 futures: 54% survive going down-right (best covers 35%); up-left 0%; up-right 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 71% survive going down-left (best covers 65%); right 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 50% survive going right (best covers 32%); down-left 0%.
Jackpot! A future after going down-left covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 3,106 variables and 8,406 clauses in 0.00 s (820 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
